title: 2 things I never give to AI
summary: On a listing video for a ₹40-crore home with 143 shots, Claude sorted everything into A-roll, B-roll, drone and close-up bins in one go. But I always cut the base A-roll and pick the music myself. That's the feel a client pays for. Here are the prompts for the parts Claude does.
steps: Run Prompt 1 on your shoot folder. It sorts clips without touching the source files.
Cut the base A-roll yourself. That's where the story is.
Run Prompt 2 for a music shortlist. Then listen and pick with your own ears.

prompts.title: 1. Sort my shoot into bins
prompts.text:
Look at every video clip in [SHOOT FOLDER].
1. List each clip: name, duration, resolution, fps, camera model (from metadata) and created time.
2. Sample 3 frames per clip (at 10%, 50% and 90%) and classify it:
   - A-roll: a person talking to camera, stable framing, longer, with speech
   - Drone: high aerial view, DJI metadata, or a sky or rooftop view
   - Close-up: a detail or macro shot filling the frame
   - B-roll: everything else that shows the place
   - Other: if you're not sure, and say why
3. In Premiere, create bins with those names in [PROJECT NAME] and import each clip into its bin. If Premiere isn't connected, write a CSV: clip, bin.
4. Never move, rename or delete the source files.
Give me a table: count and total duration per bin, plus the clips you were unsure about.

prompts.title: 2. Music shortlist (I pick the final track)
prompts.text:
Look through my music library in [MUSIC FOLDER].
The video: [TYPE, e.g. luxury home listing], length [SECONDS] s, mood [e.g. calm, premium, warm].
Give me a shortlist of [8] tracks that fit: file name, length, estimated BPM, mood, and why it fits.
Don't place music in my edit and don't download or buy anything. I will listen and choose myself.

notes: Cut the base A-roll yourself. If you give that away too, why would a client pay you?
Choose music with your own ears. Claude only shortlists.
